claims.text: The FeNiCrMn alloy is a Co-free derivative of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The as-cast Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Removing Co alters local solute-dislocation interactions in FeNiCrMn.
Removing Co increases the effective stacking-fault energy relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The increased effective stacking-fault energy reduces deformation twinning in the Co-free alloy.
Reduced twinning shifts the dominant deformation mechanism toward thermally activated dislocation glide.
Dislocation glide in the Co-free alloy is more sensitive to temperature and strain rate than the mixed slip-and-twinning response of the baseline.
The dynamic strength-ductility balance of FeNiCrMn is controlled by temperature- and rate-dependent dislocation mobility.
Local lattice distortion and altered stacking-fault energy influence dislocation density and mobility in the Co-free alloy.
Yield strength and strain hardening in FeNiCrMn are more sensitive to temperature and strain-rate variation than in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, FeNiCrMn will exhibit a more pronounced reduction in yield strength at elevated temperatures.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, FeNiCrMn will exhibit altered strain hardening under high strain rates because of thermal activation and dynamic recovery of dislocations.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi deforms through a mixture of dislocation slip and significant deformation twinning.
CoCrFeMnNi has a favorable strength-ductility balance.
The proposed mechanism applies in a single-phase solid-solution regime from room temperature to about 500 °C and from 0.001 to 1000 s^-1.
Within the stated regime, thermal activation significantly influences dislocation mobility.
A controlled comparison of identically processed FeNiCrMn and CoCrFeMnNi specimens across the specified temperatures and strain rates can distinguish the proposed mechanism.

The hypothesis is falsified if the alloys have indistinguishable temperature- and rate-dependent yield behavior, or if FeNiCrMn shows no reduction in twinning coupled to a shift toward dislocation-controlled deformation.
